### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

On native Wayland with **GNOME Mutter**, the toggle (`setIgnoreMouseEvents`) does not take effect reliably:

-When `true` is passed, Chromium does set and commit an empty input region, but Mutter may fail to send `wl_pointer.leave` if the pointer is already inside the surface. In this case, mouse events (motion, button) continue to be delivered to the overlay for several seconds or indefinitely — even when the client is committing the empty region continuously at ~60 Hz via animation.
-When `false` is passed, the reverse symptom has been observed: the restored input region may not take effect promptly on an idle surface, though this requires further confirmation.

**Cross-environment comparison**: the same build under **KWin 5.27** consistently receives wl_pointer.leave within 30–290 ms after each empty-region commit, and click pass-through succeeds reliably (3/3 attempts). This confirms the issue is specific to Mutter's handling of input region changes on surfaces that already have pointer focus.

**Supporting observations:**

- Animated surface, GNOME Mutter: empty region committed ~170 times on the correct pointer-focused surface. Two identical toggles produced opposite results — one triggered wl_pointer.leave after ~160 ms, the other received no leave and continued delivering events for 4+ seconds.
- Same binary, KWin 5.27: wl_pointer.leave received within 30–290 ms after every empty-region commit. Enter/leave balanced 19/19. Pass-through succeeded 3/3.

### Proposed Solution

_AI proposed solution removed, will post a bug report instead of feature request._

### Alternatives Considered

_AI proposed solution removed, will post a bug report instead of feature request._

### Additional Information

**Context:** Originally surfaced as a follow-up to #51769 ("fix: implement setIgnoreMouseEvents on Wayland"). The PR itself works correctly; this issue is about the residual unreliability that #51769 cannot fully address inside Electron alone.

**Root-cause analysis** (Chromium 150.0.7849.0, verified identical in `chromium/src` `main`):

- `ui/ozone/platform/wayland/host/wayland_surface.cc` `WaylandSurface::set_input_region()` only forwards directly to `wl_surface_set_input_region` when `apply_state_immediately_` is `true`. Otherwise it stores the region in `pending_state_` and waits for `ApplyPendingState()` to be called.
- `apply_state_immediately_` is only ever set to `true` from one place: `ui/ozone/platform/wayland/gpu/gl_surface_wayland.cc` — i.e., only the GL-surface path.
- `ApplyPendingState()` is invoked solely from `WaylandFrameManager` on frame submission. With no GL surface and no visual change, the compositor (or Chromium itself) may skip the frame and the input region change never lands.
- `compositor()->ScheduleFullRedraw()` schedules a paint but does not guarantee a buffer commit; if the surface is visually identical to the prior frame, the request is effectively dropped.

**Repro environment used to verify:**

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel `6.17.0-1013-azure` |
| Desktop | GNOME Shell 46.0, Mutter, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=ubuntu:GNOME` |
| Session | Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`) |
| Electron | `44.0.0-nightly.20260525` built from #51769 |
| Chromium | 150.0.7849.0 |
| GPU | None (Azure VM, `drmGetDevices2()` returns no devices, software rendering) — exposes the underlying race on the non-GL path |
| Repro app | Frameless transparent `BrowserWindow` (`frame: false, transparent: true, alwaysOnTop: true`) toggling `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true })` |
| Launch | `--no-sandbox --ozone-platform=wayland` |

**Linked PR:** #51769

---

_Investigation and writeup assisted by Claude (Anthropic), reviewed and posted by [@wehos](https://github.com/wehos)._

### Problem Description

`BrowserWindow.setIgnoreMouseEvents()` on **native Wayland** applies asynchronously and unreliably. Even after the API call returns and the JS-side state flips, the Wayland compositor may continue delivering pointer events to the surface for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds — and in some sequences it never applies at all until an unrelated event happens. This is the underlying problem #51769 worked around with `compositor()->ScheduleFullRedraw()`, but that workaround is not sufficient in two reproducible cases:

1. **Race during the "passthrough turning on" window.** If the user (or any pointer event) hits the surface in the gap between `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)` returning and the input region actually committing, the surface gets "stuck" in non-passthrough — the new region never lands.
2. **`setIgnoreMouseEvents(false)` while focused.** On a focused, idle, transparent overlay (frame:false, transparent:true), turning passthrough OFF often does nothing — the prior empty input region stays committed indefinitely until some other event jolts the compositor.

Root cause is upstream Chromium behavior, **not** Electron-side, and exists in current `main` (verified against `chromium/main` at the time of filing). See the linked Chromium issue.

### Proposed Solution

Once the linked Chromium issue is resolved, Electron inherits the fix automatically. In the meantime, two interim options for Electron to consider:

1. **Cherry-pick / carry a Chromium patch** in `patches/chromium/` that either (a) exposes `CommitNow()` on `WaylandToplevelExtension`, or (b) makes `WaylandSurface::set_input_region` flush directly when `apply_state_immediately_` is false. Either makes `setIgnoreMouseEvents` (and any other path that touches the input region without a frame cycle) work reliably without waiting on a buffer commit.
2. **No-op damage trick** at the Electron layer: after `UpdateFrameHints()` in `ElectronDesktopWindowTreeHostLinux::SetIgnoreMouseEvents`, mark a 1-pixel damage region on the compositor's root layer to force the next frame to actually submit. Less invasive but hacky.

- Polling `setShape()` (the original N.E.K.O. workaround). Works but is a per-frame timer-driven hack.
- Switching to X11 / XWayland. Not acceptable for native-Wayland use cases.

nodes.title: macos-arm64 BrowserWindow tests time out on main (since 2026-05-24)
nodes.body:
## Summary
Every `macos-arm64 / test` job (darwin + mas) has been failing on `main` since 2026-05-24. ~30 `BrowserWindow` window-management tests in `spec/api-browser-window-spec.ts` fail, all with `Timeout of 30000ms exceeded` (×3 retries): show/hide, focus/blur/z-order, minimize/maximize bounds, `visibilityState`, content protection, capturePage. The expected window event never fires — this looks like a broken window-server session in the runner, not a logic bug.

## When it started
- ✅ green — `chore: bump chromium to 150.0.7849.0 (#51733)`, run `26301533643` (05-22)
- ❌ red — `ci: unpin homebrew version (#51757)`, run `26368726651` (05-24)

## Likely cause
Two things changed between those runs:

| | green | red |
|---|---|---|
| runner image | `macos-15-arm64/20260427` | `macos-15-arm64/20260520` |
| macOS | 15.7.4 | 15.7.7 |
| Homebrew pin | present | removed (#51757) |

The **macOS 15.7.4 → 15.7.7 runner-image bump** is the likely trigger (window-server / screen-recording TCC / modal-dialog behavior). The Homebrew unpin is probably *not* the cause: the test job runs prebuilt artifacts and never invokes `brew` for anything GUI-related.

nodes.title: Child processes crash at launch in base::i18n::InitializeICUFromDataFile (ICU init CHECK fails), exit 0x80000003, Windows 11 26200
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.

### Electron Version

40.8.5

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro 25H2 (build 26200.8457)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown / not bisected

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Electron child processes (GPU, renderer, utility) initialize and the app launches normally, as it does for Chromium/Chrome and for older-Electron apps on the same machine.

### Actual Behavior

On this machine, every Electron child process aborts at the very first step of startup — before GPU init, sandbox lockdown, or logging — inside ICU initialization. The browser process is fine; only child processes die.

Symbolized stack (cdb / WinDbg, child-process following, Electron's public symbol server, exact electron.exe.pdb match):

    electron!base::i18n::InitializeICUFromDataFile     <- CHECK fails
    electron!base::i18n::InitializeICU
    electron!content::ContentMainRunnerImpl::Initialize
    electron!content::RunContentProcess
    electron!content::ContentMain
    electron!wWinMain

So `CHECK(InitializeICU())` trips -> base::ImmediateCrash -> the child exits 0x80000003 (STATUS_BREAKPOINT). The app's own log (no debugger) confirms the same code:

    child-process-gone { type: 'GPU', reason: 'crashed', exitCode: -2147483645 }   // = 0x80000003

Because the abort is this early, the child writes no log and no crash dump. The browser only sees the child vanish, counts it as a GPU crash, exhausts GPU fallback modes, and aborts via content::IntentionallyCrashBrowserForUnusableGpuProcess ("GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye."). That is why it superficially looks like a GPU problem, but the GPU is never reached.

Result: the app shows a blank window or quits on launch. Reproduces with multiple Electron 40 apps (Proton Mail 1.13.0 = Electron 40.8.5; GitHub Desktop 3.5.10 shows the identical instant-vanish, no-dump fingerprint).

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This needs no special app code to reproduce — any recent-Electron app crashes the same way on this machine, so a Fiddle would just be a default app. Happy to produce one if useful.

Evidence it is ICU init, not the GPU/driver:
- icudtl.dat is present and valid (10,822,192 bytes, correct ICU header) and the **browser** process loads that same file fine; only **child** processes fail.
- dxdiag: AMD RX 7900 XTX healthy, Direct3D feature level 12_2.
- Ruled out: HVCI off; all Exploit Protection / process mitigations NOTSET (MicrosoftSignedOnly, ProhibitDynamicCode, DisallowWin32k, etc.); no AppInit_DLLs / AppCertDlls; no AV/EDR/anti-cheat; clean DDU + several AMD driver versions; a full clean Windows reinstall.
- Scope: Chrome/Brave (Chromium) and an older-Electron app (Signal) are unaffected on this exact machine; only recent Electron (40.x) fails. So the failure is specific to Electron's child-process ICU initialization on this Windows build (26200), not core Chromium.

Versions: Electron 40.8.5, Chromium 144.0.7559.236, Windows 11 Pro 25H2 build 26200.8457, x64, AMD RX 7900 XTX driver 32.0.31007.5012.

Method caveat: the symbolized stack was captured under a debugger, but it matches the non-debugger exit code (0x80000003) and the pre-logging/pre-dump behaviour exactly, so it is the real fault.

Originally surfaced as Chromium issue 516312113 (filed under a GPU/AMD-driver premise that turned out to be a red herring). Crash logs, full symbolized stack, dxdiag, and a symbol-matched dump available on request.

### Expected Behavior

A packaged Electron app whose product name differs from "Electron" (i.e. every real-world app) should launch correctly on macOS 26 arm64.

The helper app path should be resolved at runtime using the main bundle's name — for example, by reading `CFBundleName` from `Info.plist` — so that standard packager behavior (renaming `Electron Helper.app` to `MyApp Helper.app`) works without requiring binary patching.


### Actual Behavior


The app crashes immediately on launch with exit code **133 (SIGTRAP)** and no output.

Running the binary directly from the terminal reveals the fatal error:

```
[FATAL:electron/shell/app/electron_main_delegate_mac.mm:66] Unable to find helper app
```

The Electron binary appears to resolve its helper processes using a name fixed at compile time (`Electron Helper`) rather than derived at runtime from the app bundle's `CFBundleName`. When a packager renames the helper bundles to match the product name (standard practice), the binary can no longer find them.

This was confirmed by the following test:

```bash
# Start from the unmodified node_modules Electron.app
cp -R node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app /tmp/TestApp.app

# Simulate what electron-builder does: rename helpers
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper.app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper.app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (GPU).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (GPU).app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (Plugin).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (Plugin).app"
mv "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/Electron Helper (Renderer).app" \
   "/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/Frameworks/TestApp Helper (Renderer).app"

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /tmp/TestApp.app

/tmp/TestApp.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron
# → [FATAL] Unable to find helper app  (exit 133)
```

Restoring helpers to their original `Electron Helper*.app` names makes the app launch correctly.

Additionally, the packaged binary is **byte-for-byte identical** to the original from the npm package (same SHA-256 hash), confirming it was never patched:

```bash
shasum -a 256 "dist/mac-arm64/MyApp.app/Contents/MacOS/MyApp"
# c86c2701f15ca66ba460f4cdcd7ebcab0b5133a4cc299295f02108b3754e9eed

shasum -a 256 "node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron"
# c86c2701f15ca66ba460f4cdcd7ebcab0b5133a4cc299295f02108b3754e9eed
```


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/ElRochito/f251a4231213679f31a6c97d5b8ab625

### Additional Information


**Workaround** (in electron-builder): add an `afterPack` hook that renames the helpers back to their original `Electron Helper*.app` names after packaging. See companion issue filed against [electron-builder](https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder).

**What did NOT help:**
- Setting `hardenedRuntime: false` in electron-builder config
- Setting `identity: null` to skip code signing
- Removing the quarantine attribute (`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`)
- Re-signing the bundle with `codesign --force --deep -s -`
- All FUSE flags are identical between working and failing binaries (`EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` is disabled in both)

**Suggested fix:** In `electron/shell/app/electron_main_delegate_mac.mm` around line 66, derive the helper name from `[NSBundle.mainBundle objectForInfoDictionaryKey:@"CFBundleName"]` at runtime rather than using a compile-time constant, e.g.:

```objc
NSString *bundleName = [NSBundle.mainBundle objectForInfoDictionaryKey:@"CFBundleName"];
NSString *helperName = [NSString stringWithFormat:@"%@ Helper", bundleName];
```

This would make the helper resolution robust to any product name without requiring binary patching.

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Electron applications should launch normally even if the directory contains unparseable or orphaned zombie SIDs, or gracefully handle the permission validation error without crashing the entire GPU process.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process crashes on startup with exit_code=-2147483645 and outputs "FATAL:gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc: GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye."

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

**TL;DR:** Electron apps crash with exit_code=-2147483645 because the folder's DACL contains orphaned zombie SIDs (S-1-15...). Granting permissions to `S-1-15-2-2` (ALL RESTRICTED APPLICATION PACKAGES) or running `icacls /reset` fixes the crash. This is closely related to the LPAC sandbox requirement discussed in #49143.

#### Description

Recently, on my Windows PC, many Electron-based desktop applications (such as Discord, Bitwarden, LM Studio, Postman, VS Code, etc.) crash frequently, making them completely unusable. The error messages are as follows:

```
[33240:0524/193721.652:ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:999] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[33240:0524/193721.652:FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

After searching online, I found that other users have reported the same error recently:

- liliMozi/openhanako#1083
- anthropics/claude-code#61372
- postmanlabs/postman-app-support#14149

Currently, the only temporary solution is to add the `--disable-gpu-sandbox` parameter at startup. However, this requires doing it manually every time and is not a permanent solution.

#### Hypothesis

After repeated troubleshooting and verification with AI, we ruled out hardware and driver issues. (During this time, I tried reinstalling drivers, reinstalling software, reinstalling Windows, adjusting Core Isolation and HAGS, updating BIOS, etc., but nothing worked.)

Finally, the AI identified the possible cause: an issue with the security permission list (DACL) of the application folder, which contains an unresolvable "zombie SID" (shown as "Unknown Account" in the Windows interface). This conclusion can be consistently reproduced using the following steps.

#### Reproduction Steps

Please create a clean Electron project then package, or use an existing Electron application folder directly (the following example uses VS Code with PowerShell):

1. Add a zombie SID to the application folder:

```PowerShell
icacls "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code" /grant "*S-1-15-2-999-999-999:(OI)(CI)(F)"
```

2. Run the application:

```PowerShell
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe" --verbose
```

**Expected Result**: The application will crash immediately during GPU initialization and output the following error logs:

```
[37568:0524/201836.841:ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:999] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[37568:0524/201836.841:FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:415] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
```

3. Run the following command to reset permissions and remove the zombie SID. After that, the application will work normally again:

```PowerShell
icacls "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code" /reset
```

#### Additional Context

Before submitting this issue, I researched related past reports and noticed:

* #49143

It mentions that enabling the network sandbox in newer versions might cause permission issues, requiring the following command to grant permissions:

```PowerShell
icacls <install dir> /grant *S-1-15-2-2:(OI)(CI)(RX)
```

Following this clue, I did a cross-test and made a new discovery: if both the unknown zombie SID and the `S-1-15-2-2` permission exist at the same time, the application can start successfully without crashing.

### Electron Version

42.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Ubuntu

### Operating System Version

Linux LT-IttayD 6.8.0-111-generic #111-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat Apr 11 23:16:02 UTC 2026 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux x11

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

After dismissing a window.confirm() dialog, re-focusing an input element causes the caret to blink as normal. Same behavior as Chrome (and as Electron's own dialog.showMessageBoxSync from the main process).

### Actual Behavior

After dismissing a window.confirm() dialog, the caret is invisible on any focused input. document.activeElement, document.hasFocus(), and caret-color all  report correct values, but the caret pseudo-element is never painted. Typing still inserts text. The caret reappears only after a real OS-level window-activation event (alt-tab to another window and back, opening DevTools).

Steps after loading the gist in Fiddle:
  1. Run. App opens with an input pre-focused — caret blinks.
  2. Click Trigger confirm. Native dialog appears.
  3. Click OK. The script re-focuses the input.
  4. Caret is invisible. Even after clicking in the input. 
  5. Alt-tab away and back — caret reappears.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/ittayd/7cbd32701869e526fe259dea0e520da7

### Additional Information

- Reproduces on Electron 41.0.3 and 42.2.0 (different Chromium versions, both affected).
  - Linux, X11 (XDG_SESSION_TYPE=x11), tested on GNOME.
  - Does not reproduce in Chrome with the same HTML.
  - Does not reproduce if window.confirm is replaced with dialog.showMessageBoxSync via sync IPC.
  - Possibly same root cause as #45165 (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/45165) (caret stops blinking after context menu, marked blocked/upstream)
  and #14474 (https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/14474) (input cursor invisible after navigation in webview).
  - Best guess at fix: JavaScriptDialogManager::DidCloseDialog (or the equivalent OS-modal-close path) needs to refresh Chromium's per-frame focus tracking
  before returning control to the renderer. dialog.showMessageBoxSync already handles this correctly.

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Tahoe 26.5

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Async encryption should be reliably available or unavailable.

- `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` should return `true` on macOS when Keychain is reachable (i.e. whenever `isEncryptionAvailable()` is `true` and async encryption works in another codebase)
- If async encryption truly isn't available, calling `encryptStringAsync` / `decryptStringAsync` should reject the returned promise not crash the process.


### Actual Behavior


- `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` returns `false` from a minimal repro
- Calling `encryptStringAsync()` SIGSEGVs the process with the V8 HandleScope error above.

Notably, the same `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` call returns `true` in a larger codebase on the same machine and Electron build.

```js
// safeStorageTest.js
import { app, safeStorage } from 'electron'

app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  console.log({
    isEncryptionAvailable: safeStorage.isEncryptionAvailable(),
    isAsyncEncryptionAvailable: await safeStorage.isAsyncEncryptionAvailable(),
  })
  // Crashes with V8 HandleScope error:
  await safeStorage.encryptStringAsync('secret')
  app.quit()
})
```

Run with `npx electron safeStorageTest.js`.

Output:

```
{ isEncryptionAvailable: true, isAsyncEncryptionAvailable: false }
[ERROR:electron/shell/common/node_bindings.cc:171] Fatal error in V8:
  v8::HandleScope::CreateHandle() Cannot create a handle without a HandleScope
Electron exited with signal SIGSEGV
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Notably, the same `isAsyncEncryptionAvailable()` call returns `true` in another codebase on the same machine using the same Electron build. I've tried the steps below to make the repro above work:

- Calling `safeStorage.encryptString(...)` (sync) first (works fine, but async still reports unavailable)
- Creating a hidden `new BrowserWindow({ show: false })` before the probe
- Setting `app.setName('Test')` before `whenReady`

A workaround that **does work** is an arbitrary 2 second delay. So this seems to be an initialization issue.

### Expected Behavior

P010LE textures should be importable and usable through Electron’s shared texture API on Windows.

### Actual Behavior

P010LE texture import fails on Windows when using Electron’s shared texture API.

The failure occurs during Chromium SharedImage creation because DXGI shared-handle import does not support P010 due to a missing format mapping in:

GetDXGIFormatForGMB (d3d_image_backing_factory.cc)

As a result:
- viz::MultiPlaneFormat::kP010 resolves to DXGI_FORMAT_UNKNOWN
- WebGL context is lost

Upstream fix has been proposed here:

### Electron Version

40.10.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS Sequoia 15.6.1

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Since the overlay is visually transparent and passes mouse events through, the underlying window is both visible and interactive. Its document.visibilityState should stay 'visible', no background throttling should apply, and clicks/animations should remain fully responsive.

### Actual Behavior

The underlying window's document.visibilityState becomes 'hidden' as soon as the transparent overlay covers it. Background throttling activates. Clicks (delivered through the overlay's pass-through) reach the main window but respond with noticeable latency; animations stutter.
Briefly dragging the underlying window restores 'visible', but it returns to 'hidden' once the drag ends and the overlay covers it again.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When a transparent: true BrowserWindow with mouse events set to pass through (setIgnoreMouseEvents(true)) is positioned on top of another BrowserWindow on macOS Sequoia, the underlying window's document.visibilityState flips to 'hidden' and background throttling kicks in — even though the underlying content is fully visible and interactive to the user through the overlay. 

Affected versions

Electron: 40.9.0 and later. Confirmed in 40.10.0, 41 . Confirmed not present in 40.8.5.
macOS: 15.x (Sequoia). Not reproducible on macOS 26.

Related PRs

#50579 — the change after which this regression appears. Fixes #45776 (a different occlusion scenario — windows created hidden and shown later) and incidentally removes the previous global disable that had been masking this bug.
#50712, #50713, #50715 — backports of #50579 to 42-x-y / 40-x-y / 41-x-y release branches.

nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.

### Electron Version

42.1.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (verified on 10.0.22631 and 10.0.26200)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.2.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

For `BrowserWindow({ frame: false, thickFrame: true, resizable: true })` on Windows, the on-screen HWND rect (read via `user32!GetWindowRect`) equals `screen.dipToScreenRect(win.getBounds())`. `setBounds({ x, y, width: W, height: H })` produces a visible window of `W × H` DIP at `(x, y)`. This held through Electron `41.3.0`.

### Actual Behavior

Starting in `41.3.0` (backport of #50706 via #50863) and `42.0.0` (via #50864), the HWND extends outward from `getBounds()` by `SM_CXSIZEFRAME + SM_CXPADDEDBORDER` DIP on **left, right, and bottom**, and by `0` on **top**. `setBounds({ x, y, width: W, height: H })` produces a visible window of `(W + 16) × (H + 8)` DIP at `(x - 8, y)` at 100% DPI (scales with DPI). `getBounds()`, `getNormalBounds()`, and `getContentBounds()` continue to return the original logical (inset-subtracted) rect, so the `getBounds() ↔ HWND` identity is broken on this window class. No constructor option, runtime flag, or JS API to query the inset or restore pre-41.3 behavior. 

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/gdavidkov/c8c466109c009ff195f1abdcb68362a9

### Additional Information

### How the break looks in numbers

Same `BrowserWindow` options, same display, **measured locally** with the repro at the bottom of this issue:

| Observation | Electron 41.2.0 (last working) | Electron 41.3.0 / 42.1.0 (same input) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asymmetricInsetPhysical` @ 100% DPI | `{0, 0, 0, 0}` | `{left:8, top:0, right:8, bottom:8}` | new inset |
| `asymmetricInsetPhysical` @ 137.5% DPI | `{0, 0, 0, 0}` | `{left:12, top:0, right:12, bottom:11}` | new inset (scales with DPI) |
| Visible window width for `setBounds(w:500)` | 500 DIP | 516 DIP | **+16 DIP** |
| Visible window height for `setBounds(h:400)` | 400 DIP | 408 DIP | **+8 DIP** |
| `getBounds()` vs HWND rect | identical | HWND = bounds outset by `TLBR(0, T, T, T)` | identity broken |
| Center of `getBounds()` vs HWND center on Y | identical | logical center is `T/2` above HWND center | **−4 DIP** |
| `setBounds(display.workArea)` fills `workArea` | yes | overflows `workArea` by `T` DIP on L / R / B | window leaves work area |

### Source of the change

Introduced by **#50706** *"fix: external resize hit targets for frameless windows on Windows"* (shipped as #50864), with follow-up regression fix in **#51252 / #51296**. The relevant code in [`shell/browser/ui/views/win_frame_view.cc@v42.1.0`](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/v42.1.0/shell/browser/ui/views/win_frame_view.cc):

```cpp
gfx::Insets WinFrameView::RestoredFrameBorderInsets() const {
  if (window_->has_frame() || !window_->has_thick_frame() ||
      !window_->IsResizable())
    return {};

  const int thickness =
      display::win::GetScreenWin()->GetSystemMetricsInDIP(SM_CXSIZEFRAME) +
      display::win::GetScreenWin()->GetSystemMetricsInDIP(SM_CXPADDEDBORDER);
  return gfx::Insets::TLBR(0, thickness, thickness, thickness);
}
```

- [#50706](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50706) — the fix on `main`
- [#50863](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50863) — backport to `41-x-y` (shipped in `41.3.0`)
- [#50864](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50864) — backport to `42-x-y` (shipped in `42.0.0`)
- [#51244](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51244) — regression introduced by #50706
- [#51252](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51252) — regression fix on `main`
- [#51296](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51296) — regression-fix backport
- [#51287](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/51287) — `fix: remove insets on fullscreen windows on Windows` (related follow-up)

### Electron Version

42.x.y

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

GHA Windows 2022

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

41.5.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

Native modules rebuilt against Electron 42 headers on Windows with MSVC should not fail to build

### Actual Behavior

Electron 42 ships a `cppgc/heap.h` header that unconditionally calls:

```cpp
__builtin_frame_address(0)
```

MSVC does not support `__builtin_frame_address`, so the build fails with an error like:
```
error C3861: '__builtin_frame_address': identifier not found
```

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This may need fixing upstream in Node but thought I would open here first for visibility.

Users are adding their own workarounds to get their native modules building with Electron v42:
https://github.com/zwfthcks/memoryjs/pull/2
